titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spells 43, 89, 91 and 92
part: Spells 43, 89, 91 and 92 — keeping the head; the ba and the shadow free to come and go (Plates 17–18)
about: Four short spells on Plates 17 and 18 of Ani's papyrus, written after Spells 44, 45, 46, 50 and 93. Spell 43 keeps the dead man's head on his body, as the head of Osiris was given back to him. Spells 89, 91 and 92 are for the ba, the part of the person that leaves the tomb by day: that it may come back to its corpse and rest on its mummy, that it may not be shut in at the gates of the West, and that the tomb may be opened to it and to the shadow so that the dead man goes forth by day. Many words are rare or obscure and several signs in Budge's print are uncertain; the notes say where a reading is doubtful.

sentences.l: spell · of · not · letting · be-cut-off · the-head · of-a-man · from-him · in · the-necropolis
sentences.i: Spell for not letting a man's head be cut off from him in the necropolis.
sentences.n: Spell 43 begins. The papyrus writes rꜣ n tm rdit šꜥd tp in red, then s in black, m-ꜥ·f m in red again, and ẖrt-nṯr in black. rꜣ n 'spell of' is the mouth with its stroke and water n, as in every title. tm is t, the sledge tm (U15, printed with cross-hatching like a ladder) and the owl m as complement, the t written first: the negative verb 'not to do', whose verb follows in the negatival complement. rdit is the mouth r, the arm (D36; no loaf is printed) and t: 'not letting'. šꜥd 'be cut off' is the pool š (coded N37, approximate), the arm ꜥ and the hand d, with a hatched stick (coded M44, approximate, as in the earlier writings of this word) and the knife as classifiers of cutting; after rdit it is taken as the passive sḏm (the verb with no ending of its own), with tp s as its subject, 'letting a man's head be cut off'; read as an active sḏm·f it would make the head the one that cuts. tp 'head' is the head in profile with its stroke. s 'man' is the bolt s, a stroke and the seated man. m-ꜥ·f 'from him' is the owl m with the arm joined to it, and ·f. ẖrt-nṯr 'the necropolis' is the flag nṯr written first, the loop r (coded D21, approximate) and the block ẖr (T28). Beheading was a fate of the damned in the world below: the dead man must keep his head on his body.

sentences.l: said · by · the-Osiris · Ani · (Ani) · I · the-Great-One · son · of-the-Great-One · Flame · son · of-Flame
sentences.i: Said by the Osiris Ani: I am the Great One, son of the Great One; I am Flame, son of Flame.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ꜣny twice (Budge prints '(sic)' under the second, after his line numeral 2); read it once. ḏd in N 'said by N' is written here in black: the cobra and the hand in one ligature, then water n alone, with no reed (Budge reads àn): the agent particle in, written without its reed, as in the Address after Spell 125. wsir is the low seat (coded Q2, approximate) over the eye, with no god classifier. ink 'I' is the pot in (W24) with k and the seated man: ink N 'I am N'. wr 'great one' is the swallow wr (G36) with r as complement and a man standing with a tall staff (coded A21, approximate) as classifier, the sign of a person of rank. sꜣ 'son' is the pintail duck sꜣ with its stroke, and the second wr is written as the first: sꜣ wr, a direct genitive, 'son of the Great One'. nsrt 'flame' is water n and the bolt s, printed small under a long sign whose end hooks down; that sign has no good code and is coded F20 (the tongue, ns), approximate, the nearest sign that carries Budge's nes-; read so, water n and the bolt are its complements. Then r, t and the brazier with a flame (coded Q7, approximate) as classifier. sꜣ nsrt is 'son of Flame'. The speaker claims the descent of a god: the son is what the father was.

sentences.l: was-given · to-him · head-his · after · was-cut-off-it
sentences.i: His head was given to him after it had been cut off.
sentences.n: Budge prints erṭāi-nef as one group (his numeral 3 is printed inside it); it is split here into rdy and n·f (q re-indexed). rdy is the mouth r, the arm (D36, no loaf) and two reeds y: the passive sḏm of rdi 'give', 'was given', with the weak ending y written out. n·f 'to him' is water n and the viper ·f. The same group could be read as the sḏm·n·f rdi·n·f 'he gave (his head)', as in Spell 61, but its ·f would then refer to no one named before it; the passive, with n·f 'to him', is taken. tp·f 'his head' is the head with its stroke and ·f. m-ḫt 'after' is the owl m, a branch with a curled end, the sign ḫt (coded M3, approximate), with ḫ and t as complements, and the walking legs (coded D54, approximate) as classifier: the compound preposition, here before a verb. šꜥd·tw·f is written as in the title, with the low hooked sign (U15) after the knife as a further classifier (this low sign recurs in the part where Budge reads no letter; it is taken as a classifier throughout, but its value is not clear), then t and the chick w, and ·f: the sḏm·tw·f, the passive, 'it was cut off'. The god whose head was cut off and given back is Osiris, whose body Seth cut apart and Isis and her helpers made whole again.

sentences.l: not · shall-be-taken-away · the-head · of · Osiris · from-him
sentences.i: The head of Osiris shall not be taken away from him.
sentences.n: nn is the negative arms (coded D35, approximate) and water n: nn with the sḏm·f, the negative of the future, 'shall not'. nḥm·tw is water n, the bowl ḥm with its three-pointed rim (coded N41, approximate) and the bar m (Aa15) as complement, the low hooked sign (U15) as classifier, then t and the chick w: nḥm 'take away' in the passive sḏm·tw·f. tp n wsir 'the head of Osiris' uses the genitive n (water n). m-ꜥ·f 'from him' as in the title. The head of the god is safe: the speaker will say the same of his own.

sentences.l: not · shall-be-taken-away · the-head · of · the-Osiris · Ani · from-him
sentences.i: The head of the Osiris Ani shall not be taken away from him.
sentences.n: The sentence is repeated with the name of Ani. nn nḥm·tw as before; here the water n, the bowl and the bar are printed one over the other. Budge's line numeral 4 stands before ꜣny, which has a single stroke after the reeds in place of the seated man. What is said of Osiris is now said of the Osiris Ani: the dead man is safe because he is the god.

sentences.l: (iw)-I · knit-together-am-I · set-right(?)-am-I · young-am-I
sentences.i: I am knit together, I am set in order(?), I am young again.
sentences.n: iw·i is the reed, the coil w (Z7) and the seated man ·i: iw opens a statement, and with the stative it states a condition. Three statives with the ending ·kwi 'I' follow. In each the papyrus prints t between the basket k and the chick w (Budge reads no t, and gives the ending as kuà); the t is not read. ṯs·kwi 'I am knit together' is the knot ṯs (S24) with the coil w and the low hooked sign (U15) as classifier; the coil, which belongs to the writing ṯsw seen in Spell 93, is not read here. ṯs is 'tie, knot', of a body whose joints are bound together again. mꜣꜥ·kwi is the sickle mꜣ lying over the arm ꜥ, with the papyrus roll: the stative of mꜣꜥ 'be true, right', taken as 'I am set right, in order'; Budge has 'made myself whole and sound', and the sense here is doubtful. rnp·kwi 'I am young' is r, n and p, the reed i, the palm-rib rnp (M4) and a seated child with a hand to the mouth (coded A17, approximate) as classifiers: rnpi 'be young, become young again'. Here the stative ending is k, t and w, with no seated man (Budge brackets the [à] in his transliteration only). The dead man's body is bound up, made whole and young again, as the body of Osiris was.

sentences.l: I · Osiris · it-is · lord · of-eternity
sentences.i: I am Osiris, the lord of eternity.
sentences.n: ink wsir pw 'I am Osiris': ink with a noun, and pw 'it is' after the noun, as in a nominal sentence (ink … pw). nb 'lord' is the basket nb. nḥḥ 'eternity' is written with the wick ḥ twice and the sun between them, as in the Hymn to Ra: ḥḥ, the word for endless time, its n not written. Spell 43 ends with the claim that makes it work: the speaker is Osiris, whose head was given back to him.

sentences.l: spell · of · letting · join · the-ba · corpse-its · in · the-necropolis
sentences.i: Spell for letting the ba join its corpse in the necropolis.
sentences.n: Spell 89 begins, and Budge's line numerals start again at 1. The papyrus writes rꜣ n rdit dmi in red; bꜣ ẖꜣt·f m ẖrt-nṯr is black. rdit is the mouth r, t and the arm (D36, no loaf), the t printed above the arm, as in Spell 54. The next word is the hand d, the milk jug in its net (W19), the sign mi, with the reed i as complement and the papyrus roll: dmi 'touch, join, be joined to', in the sḏm·f after rdit, with bꜣ as its subject (Budge: ṭemà, 'be united'). bꜣ 'the ba' is the jabiru bꜣ (G29) with the small bowl (R7) printed at its foot and not read, as in Spells 26 and 61; Budge's tiny tick above the bird is not coded. ẖꜣt·f 'its corpse' is the belly of an animal ẖ (coded F32, approximate), the vulture ꜣ and t, with the flesh sign (coded F51, approximate) as classifier, and ·f. No preposition stands between bꜣ and ẖꜣt·f: dmi takes its object directly. The ba, the part of the person that moves freely, flies out of the tomb by day and must find the body again.

sentences.l: said · by · the-Osiris · Ani · O · Innitu(?) · O · Runner · this · who-is-in · hall-his
sentences.i: Said by the Osiris Ani: O Innitu(?)! O this Runner, who is in his hall!
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in in red. ḏd in N 'said by N', as before; here in is the reed over water n. i 'O' is the reed with the man raising a hand to his mouth (A2): the call that opens an address. The first name is the sign in, a small ring on two spread legs (coded W25, approximate), water n twice, two reeds, t and the chick w, with the seated god as classifier (Budge: Ànnitu); it is not met elsewhere in the published parts, its make-up is not clear, and it is given here in the rule-based form Innitu. pḥrry 'runner' is p and the wick ḥ, the hindquarters of a lion pḥ (coded F22, approximate) carrying the same two sounds, r twice and two reeds y, with a striding man carrying something over his shoulder (coded A24, approximate) and the seated god as classifiers: a noun from pḥrr 'run'. pw after it is the demonstrative 'this', taken with the vocative, 'O you Runner'. imy 'who is in' is the crossed planks im with m as complement and two strokes y. sḥ·f 'his hall' is a booth on a pole (O22, approximate), the sign sḥ, after a double-arched shrine (coded O21, approximate) printed before it as classifier, with a stroke and ·f. Which gods are meant is not known; both are called on to send the ba home.

sentences.l: god · great · may-give-you · come · to-me · ba-my · from · place · any · which-it(-is) · there
sentences.i: Great god, grant that my ba may come to me from any place where it is.
sentences.n: Budge's line numeral 2 stands before imy in the line above. Budge spaces nṯr and ꜥꜣ as two words, and they are kept apart: nṯr 'god' is the flag with the seated god, ꜥꜣ 'great' the lozenge-tipped column (O29). di·k 'may you give, grant' is the arm holding a conical loaf (D37), the sign di, with the low hooked sign (U15) printed under it as classifier, and ·k: the sḏm·f of rdi used for a wish. Budge prints itu-nà as one group; it is split here into iwt and n·i (q re-indexed). iwt is the walking legs iw, t and the chick w, with the walking legs again as classifier: the sḏm·f of iwi 'come' after rdi, which this verb forms with t, 'that (my ba) come'. n·i 'to me' is water n and the seated man. bꜣ·i 'my ba' is the jabiru with the bowl at its foot and ·i. m bw nb nty·f im 'from any place where it is': bw 'place' is the foot b and the chick w; nb 'any' the basket; nty·f im, 'which it (is) there', is the relative nty with ·f and the adverb im, the usual way of saying 'wherever it is'.

sentences.l: if · there-is-delay · let-be-brought · to-me · ba-my · from · place · any · which-it(-is) · there
sentences.i: If there is delay, let my ba be brought to me from any place where it is.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes nn·tw; read in·tw. ir 'if' is the reed and the mouth r. wḏfꜣw 'there is delay' is the chick w, the cobra ḏ with the viper f tucked under its body, the vulture ꜣ and the chick w, with a duck with a raised tail (coded G39, approximate) and the small ring on two spread legs (coded W25, approximate) as classifiers: a writing of wḏf 'delay, tarry' with ꜣ, used without a subject, 'if (it) delays', 'if there is delay' (Budge: ut'efau). Budge prints ànen-tu-nà as one group; it is split here into in·tw and n·i (q re-indexed). in·tw is two water lines, t and the chick w: the verb ini 'bring', written with water n doubled and without the reed, in the passive sḏm·tw·f, 'let (my ba) be brought'. n·i 'to me' as before. Budge's line numeral 3 stands before bꜣ·i. bw 'place' is written here with a stroke after the foot and no chick. The rest is said as in the line before.

sentences.l: find-you · O-Eye · of-Horus · stand-you · (then) · like · those · of-Osiris(?) · not · lie-down
sentences.i: When you find (it)(?), Eye of Horus, stand up like those of Osiris(?) who do not lie down.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes nfmy; read nfꜣy. gm·k is the ibis gm (coded G28, approximate) with the owl m as complement, the roll and ·k: 'you find', a sḏm·f with no object written (Budge supplies '[If] … [me]'); the sense of the clause is doubtful. irt ḥr 'Eye of Horus' is the eye with t and a stroke and the falcon, here called on. ꜥḥꜥ·ṯi is the mast ꜥḥꜥ (P6) with the arm ꜥ as complement and the walking legs, then the tether ṯ and the reed: ꜥḥꜥ 'stand, stand up' with the ending ·ṯi, the old spelling of the stative ·ti, here addressed to the Eye (a feminine noun) as a command (Budge: āḥā-θà). r·k, the mouth r and ·k, is the word that follows a command to strengthen it, 'you (then)'; its k does not agree with the feminine Eye. mi 'like' is the milk jug mi with i. nfꜣy 'those' is water n, the viper f, then the owl m (Budge prints '(sic)' above it) where the same phrase in line 7 has the vulture ꜣ, two strokes y, and a road with shrubs (coded N31, approximate) as classifier: taken as a demonstrative, 'those'. wsir is followed by the vulture ꜣ, the seated god and a stroke; the vulture is not read, and it may be the ꜣ the scribe left out of nfꜣy. Budge reads Àusàra, 'who are like Osiris'; 'those of Osiris', those who belong to the god, is a guess. n sḏr 'who do not lie down': n is water n, the negative, and sḏr is the bolt s, a bundle with a hatched top (coded M36, approximate), the sign ḏr, with r as complement, and a lion-legged bier (coded A55, approximate) as classifier: sḏr 'lie down, sleep'. Those who never lie down are perhaps the stars that never set.

sentences.l: not · lies-down · the-Osiris · Ani · true-of-voice · true-of-voice · in · Heliopolis · the-land · in-which · thousands · of · joinings(?)
sentences.i: The Osiris Ani does not lie down, true of voice, true of voice, in Heliopolis, the land in which are thousands of joinings(?).
sentences.n: Budge's line numeral 4 stands after n. sḏrw is written as sḏr in the line above, with the chick w and a stroke: the same verb, with Ani as its subject; the w may mark a passive or another form, and Budge has 'let lie down'. mꜣꜥ-ḫrw is written twice, both times short, the plinth mꜣꜥ (Aa11) over the oar ḫrw (P8), without the sickle. 'True of voice' is said of one whose words were found true in the judgement, vindicated. iwnw 'Heliopolis' is the pillar iwn (O28) with the pot nw and the town sign (Budge: Ànnu). tꜣ 'the land' is the land sign (coded N16, approximate). m 'in (which)' is the owl. ḫꜣ 'thousands' is the lotus leaf ḫꜣ (M12), the sign of the number 1000, with a stroke and plural strokes. dmi is written as in the title (hand d, milk jug mi, reed, roll): taken as a noun, 'joinings, unions', of bas with their bodies (Budge: ṭemà, 'unions'); the sense is doubtful. Heliopolis, the city of the sun, is here a place where the dead are joined to their bas.

sentences.l: (iw)-he · (shall)-fetch · for-me · ba-my · spirit-my · vindication-my · with-him · from · place · every · which-it(-is) · there
sentences.i: He shall fetch(?) for me my ba, my spirit and my vindication, with him, from every place where it is.
sentences.n: iw·f is the reed, the chick w and ·f. Budge prints θet-nà as one group; it is split here into iṯ and n·i (q re-indexed). iṯ 'take, fetch' is the tether ṯ lying over the walking legs, the house's coding (V13 + D54) of the sign iṯ, with t and the low hooked sign (U15) as classifier (Budge: θet). iw·f with a bare infinitive is taken as iw·f (r) iṯ, the future 'he shall fetch', with r not written; 'he' may be the keeper of the sky in the next line. Taken instead as the sḏm·n·f iṯ·n·i, 'I have taken', the line would begin with an unexplained iw·f. bꜣ·i 'my ba' as before; Budge's tick over the bird is not coded. ꜣḫ·i 'my spirit' is the crested ibis ꜣḫ with a seated long-wigged figure holding a flail (coded A52, approximate) for ·i; the ꜣḫ is the dead person as an effective, shining spirit. mꜣꜥ-ḫrw·i 'my vindication' is the plinth and oar with the seated man; Budge's numeral 5 is printed inside the word. ḥnꜥ·f 'with him' is the wick ḥ, water n and the arm ꜥ, and ·f. m bw nb nty·f im as before ('every' for 'any'). The ba, the spirit and the verdict of the judgement are the three things the dead man must have with him.

sentences.l: look · (then) · keeper · of-the-sky · for · ba-my
sentences.i: Look out, keeper of the sky, for my ba!
sentences.n: nw 'look, see' is the adze-like sign nw (coded U19, approximate) with water n, the pot nw and the chick w as complements, the group with which Spell 93 writes nwd and nwḥ; Budge reads ennu, giving the water n a sound of its own, and in Spell 17 the same group writes nn 'these', which gives no sentence here. It is taken as the imperative, strengthened by r·k as in the line before (Budge: ennu erek, 'seeth therefore'). iry 'keeper' is the reed, r and two strokes y, with the herdsman holding a stick (A47), the roll and a dotted stroke as classifiers: the nisba of r, 'one belonging to', as in iry-ꜥꜣ 'doorkeeper'. pt 'the sky' is p with the sky sign and the seated god, its t not written. n bꜣ·i 'for my ba': the preposition n.

sentences.l: if · there-is-delay · (then)-have-let-you · see · ba-my · corpse-my
sentences.i: If there is delay, (then) you have let(?) my ba see my corpse.
sentences.n: ir wḏfꜣw 'if there is delay' as before; Budge's line numeral 6 is printed after the first chick, and the ring on legs is not written here. rdi·n·k is the mouth r and the arm (no loaf), water n and ·k: the sḏm·n·f of rdi, 'you have let' (Budge: erṭā-nek, 'grant thou'); after a clause with ir one would expect a command or a wish, and the form is doubtful. mꜣꜣ 'see' is the eye with the sickle mꜣ joined to it in one ligature and the vulture ꜣ twice, the eye written first as classifier: the sḏm·f after rdi, with bꜣ·i as its subject. ẖꜣt·i 'my corpse' is the belly ẖ, ꜣ and t, with the lion-legged bier (coded A55, approximate) as classifier, and ·i. To see its body again is what the ba asks for in this spell.

sentences.l: find-you · O-Eye · of-Horus · stand-you · (then) · like · those
sentences.i: When you find (it)(?), Eye of Horus, stand up like those (…).
sentences.n: The words of line 3 are said again. Here gm·k is the ibis (G28, approximate) with the bar m (Aa15) and a flat roll (Y1); irt ḥr, ꜥḥꜥ·ṯi r·k and mi as before. Budge's numeral 7 stands before mi. nfꜣy is written correctly here, with the vulture ꜣ. The phrase breaks off after it: nothing like 'of Osiris who do not lie down' follows, and the next words begin a new address (Budge gives one braced English line for both passages).

sentences.l: O · gods · who-tow · in · the-boat · of · the-lord · of-millions · who-bring · (to)-the-sky(?) · of · the-Duat
sentences.i: O gods who tow in the boat of the lord of millions, who bring (it) to the sky(?) of the Duat,
sentences.n: i 'O' as before. nṯrw 'gods' is the flag three times with the seated god and a stroke. stꜣw 'who tow' is the bolt s, t, a small cup (coded W10, approximate, as in štꜣ elsewhere in the papyrus, where it carries no sound), the vulture ꜣ and the chick w, with a rope with a loop (coded V2, approximate), the sign of hauling, the walking legs and plural strokes as classifiers: the participle of stꜣ 'drag, tow' (Budge: setau, 'who row'). wiꜣ 'the boat' is w, the reed and ꜣ with a boat (coded P1, approximate). nb ḥḥ 'the lord of millions' is the basket nb and the god with raised arms ḥḥ (C11), the sign of a million, with two strokes and the seated god: 'lord of millions (of years)', the sun god. inyw 'who bring' is the sign in (W25, approximate) with water n, two reeds and the chick w, and a stroke: the participle of ini (Budge: àniu, 'who lead'). Budge's numeral 8 stands before ḥrt, which is the face ḥr, r and t with the sky sign (coded N1, approximate): ḥrt 'the sky, what is above'; no preposition is written before it, and it is taken as the place to which the boat is brought. n dwꜣt 'of the Duat' is the genitive n and the star dwꜣ with ꜣ, t and a house sign (coded O1, approximate) as classifier. The gods who haul the sun's boat bring it through the Duat, the world below through which it passes by night.

sentences.l: who-clear · the-ways · of · Nu · who-usher-in · the-bas · into · the-mummies
sentences.i: who clear the ways of Nu, who usher the bas into the mummies:
sentences.n: sḥryw 'who clear, who drive (all) away' is the bolt s, the face ḥr with r as complement, two reeds and the chick w: the participle of sḥri, the causative of ḥr 'be far' (Budge: seḥeriu, 'who make it to pass over'). wꜣwt 'the ways' is the road with shrubs (coded N31, approximate) with plural strokes. nw 'Nu', the water of the beginning, is water n, a circle with a rosette (coded O49, approximate) where the pot nw is expected, a stroke, an open basin (coded N37, approximate) and a rearing snake (coded I12, approximate) as classifiers. stknyw 'who usher in' is s, t, k and n, two reeds and the chick w, with the walking legs and plural strokes: the participle of stkn 'bring near, usher in', the causative of tkn 'come near' (Budge: 'who make to enter'). bꜣw 'the bas' is the jabiru with the bowl and a dotted stroke. r 'into' is the mouth r. sꜥḥw 'the mummies' is s, the arm ꜥ, the wick ḥ and the chick w, with the long-wigged seated figure holding a flail (coded A52, approximate) and a stroke: sꜥḥ, the noble body of the dead, the mummy. The gods who bring the bas back to their bodies are the ones asked to help.

sentences.l: the-hands-your · filled · holding · straightness(?)-your · grasp(?)-your · holding · staffs-your · drive-off-you · the-enemy
sentences.i: Your hands are full, holding your straightness(?); your grasp(?) holds your staffs: drive off the enemy!
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ꜣmm-f-tn; read ꜣmm·tn. Budge's numeral 9 stands before ꜥwy·tn 'your hands', two arms ꜥ with a stroke between them, the dual written by doubling the sign, and ·tn (t, water n, plural strokes). mḥ 'filled' is the sign mḥ (coded V22, approximate) with the roll: the stative used with a noun subject. ẖr 'holding, carrying' is the block ẖr (T28) with r: the preposition 'under', used of what a hand carries. ꜥqꜣ·tn is the arm ꜥ, the hill q, the vulture ꜣ, two slanting strokes, the roll and a stroke, with ·tn: ꜥqꜣ 'straight, exact', here as a noun, 'your exactness, your straight (cords?)'; the gods who tow hold something straight, perhaps the towrope, but the sense is doubtful (Budge: āqa-ten, 'your rectitude'). ꜣmm 'grasp' is the vulture ꜣ and the owl m twice, with a fist (coded D49, approximate) as classifier; the viper f between it and ·tn has no place in the word and is not read (Budge: amem-f-ten, 'ye grasp it'); read as ꜣmm·f tn, 'he grasps you', it would not fit the parallel of the line. ẖr as before. mꜥt·tn 'your staffs' is the owl m with the arm ꜥ in one ligature, t, a straight-sided pot (coded W24, approximate) and a shaft forking at its foot (coded S40, approximate) as classifiers, and ·tn: a word for staves or sceptres not otherwise met (Budge: māta-ten, 'your sceptres'); the reading is doubtful. dr·tn 'drive off' is the hand d and r with the low hooked sign and a stroke, and ·tn: dr 'drive away, expel', the sḏm·f used as a command, 'may you drive off' (Budge: ṭer-ten, 'destroy ye'). ḫfty 'the enemy' is ḫ, the viper f and t with five small curls (coded Z7, approximate), perhaps a compressed classifier of enemies; the y is not written. The towing gods are armed to keep off Apep and the enemies of the sun.

sentences.l: rejoices · the-boat · proceeds · the-god · great · in · peace
sentences.i: The boat rejoices; the great god proceeds in peace.
sentences.n: Budge's line 10 begins. ḥꜥ 'rejoice' is the wick ḥ crossed by the arm ꜥ in one ligature, a stroke and a man with both arms raised (A28), the sign of joy: the sḏm·f of ḥꜥꜥ with its noun subject after it, its second ꜥ not written. wiꜣ 'the boat' is w and the reed with a boat with a raised cabin (coded P3, approximate), its ꜣ not written. wḏꜣ 'proceed, go on' is the chick w and a tall tapering sign (coded U28, approximate) for ḏꜣ, with ꜣ and the walking legs (Budge: ut'a). nṯr ꜥꜣ 'the great god' as before, and m ḥtp 'in peace' is the owl m and the offering mat ḥtp with t and p. The sun god's voyage goes on unharmed.

sentences.l: lo · your-letting · come-forth · ba · this · of · the-Osiris · Ani · true-of-voice · before · the-gods · true-of-voice · under(?) · the-ḫpd(?) · of-you
sentences.i: See, you are to let this ba of the Osiris Ani come forth, true of voice before the gods, true of voice in your presence(?),
sentences.n: isw 'lo, see' is the reed, the folded cloth s and the chick w: the particle is, with w (Budge: àsu, 'Behold'). rdit·tn is the mouth r, t and the arm (no loaf), with ·tn; the t of ·tn is Budge's restoration in square brackets. It is taken as the infinitive rdit with ·tn as its subject, 'your letting'; read as the sḏm·f rdi·tn, 'may you let', the sense is the same. pr 'come forth' is the house pr with r and the walking legs: the sḏm·f after rdi. bꜣ pn 'this ba' is the jabiru with the bowl, and p and n. ꜣny has the seated long-wigged figure with the flail (coded A52, approximate) as classifier. mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice' is twice written short. ḫr nṯrw 'before the gods' is the placenta ḫ and r, the preposition used of persons, and the flag three times. ẖr 'under' is the block with r. The next word is ḫ, p, the small flesh sign (coded F51, approximate), the hand d and three strokes: ḫpd, a word not identified here (Budge: χepṭ, 'your persons'). n·tn after it is water n and ·tn, the t of ·tn again restored by Budge; Budge prints n and [te]n as two groups, and they are joined here as n·tn 'of you' (q re-indexed). Taken with Budge, ẖr ḫpd n·tn is 'in your presence'; the reading is doubtful.

sentences.l: from · the-horizon · eastern · of · the-sky · to · follow · to · the-place · under-him(?) · of · yesterday · in · peace · (twice) · to · the-West
sentences.i: from the eastern horizon of the sky, to follow (the god) to his place(?) of yesterday, in peace (Twice.) to the West.
sentences.n: m 'from' is the owl. ꜣḫt 'horizon' is the hill with the rising sun ꜣḫ (N27) with t and a house sign (coded O1) as classifier. iꜣbtt 'eastern' is the standard of the east iꜣb (coded R15, approximate) with b as complement, t twice and the hill-country sign: the feminine, agreeing with ꜣḫt. nt pt 'of the sky' is the genitive nt, written n and t for the feminine, and pt. r šms 'to follow' is r with the infinitive: the sign šms (coded T18, approximate) with s and the walking legs. r bw 'to the place' as before. ẖr·f is the block ẖr with r and ·f: 'under him, in his keeping'; Budge has 'where he was', and the sense is doubtful. n sf 'of yesterday' is the genitive n and sf, the folded cloth s and the viper f with the sun as classifier of time. m ḥtp sp sn 'in peace, (twice)': the threshing floor sp with two upright strokes tells the reader to say m ḥtp twice. ḫr imntt 'to the West' is ḫ and r, and the West, the feather sign imnt with t twice and the hill sign. The ba goes out with the sun at dawn and comes back with it at evening to the West, where the dead lie.

sentences.l: may-see-it · body-its · may-rest-it · upon · mummy-its
sentences.i: May it see its body; may it rest upon its mummy.
sentences.n: Budge's line 12 begins. mꜣꜣ·f 'may it see' is the eye with the sickle and two vultures, as before, and ·f: the sḏm·f for a wish, 'it' being the ba (Budge: 'he'). ẖt·f 'its body' is the belly ẖ and t, with an oval crossed by a line (coded Aa2, approximate; perhaps the flesh sign F51) as classifier, and ·f: ẖt 'belly, body', written without the ꜣ of ẖꜣt 'corpse' in the title (Budge: χat-f). ḥtp·f 'may it rest' is the offering mat with t and p, and ·f. ḥr 'upon' is the face with its stroke. sꜥḥ·f 'its mummy' is s, the arm ꜥ and the wick ḥ, with a standing mummy (A53) as classifier, and ·f. The ba comes down to rest on the body, as the vignettes show it, a human-headed bird over the mummy.

sentences.l: not · shall-perish-it · not · shall-be-destroyed-it · of · the-body · for · ever
sentences.i: It shall never perish, and its body shall never be destroyed, for ever.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes sḥk·f; read sk·f. The papyrus writes ḥbtm·f; read ḥtm·f. n is the negative arms alone (coded D35, approximate). n with the sḏm·f is strictly the negative of the past or of what cannot happen ('it does not, cannot perish'); the arms alone also write nn in this papyrus, and the clause is taken, like nn nḥm·tw in Spell 43, as the negative of the future. sk 'perish' is the folded cloth s and the basket k, with the sparrow, the sign of bad things, as classifier, and ·f; the twisted wick ḥ printed between s and k has no place in the word (Budge reads sek). ḥtm·f 'it shall be destroyed' is the wick ḥ, a tall upright with a foot (coded D58, approximate, so read as b), the sledge tm (U15, approximate) and the sparrow, with ·f: the sledge carries the tm of ḥtm, and the upright, which would give b, is not read. Budge's ḥetem agrees. n ḏt is the genitive n and ḏt 'body' (the cobra ḏ, t and a stroke): 'of the body', taken here with ḥtm·f, 'its body is not destroyed'. n ḏt 'for ever' is n and ḏt 'everlastingness', written with the land sign (coded N16, approximate). The two words ḏt, 'body' and 'ever', are written with the same two signs and told apart by their classifiers.

sentences.l: to-be-said · over · a-ba · of · gold · inlaid · with · precious-stone · placed · for · a-man · (on)-breast-his · Osiris
sentences.i: To be said over a ba of gold inlaid with precious stone, placed for a man on his breast. Osiris (…).
sentences.n: The rubric. The papyrus writes ḏd ḥr bꜣ n nbw mḥ m ꜥꜣt rdiw n in red, s in black, and šnbt·f wsir in red. ḏd 'to be said' is the cobra and the hand in one ligature, with a short stroke set high over three strokes; the strokes may stand for mdw 'words', as in ḏd mdw 'words to be said', the heading of a recitation (Budge: t'eṭ). ḥr 'over' is the face. bꜣ is the jabiru with the bowl. nbw 'gold' is the collar of beads nbw (S12) with plural strokes. mḥ 'inlaid, filled' is the sign mḥ (coded V22, approximate) with a roll: the stative, 'filled'. m ꜥꜣt 'with precious stone' is the owl and ꜥꜣt, the column ꜥꜣ (O29) lying flat, t, a single slanting stroke (coded Z5, approximate) and a stroke. rdiw 'placed' is r, the arm (no loaf) and the chick w: the passive participle of rdi, agreeing with bꜣ. n s 'for a man' is water n and s, the bolt, a stroke and the man. ḥr is not written before šnbt·f 'his breast', which is the loop šn (coded V7, approximate) with n, the foot b, t and the flesh sign (coded F51, approximate), and ·f. wsir 'Osiris' stands at the end without a name after it; it may be the start of a name left unwritten, as at the end of Spell 45. Amulets of a ba-bird in gold were laid on the breast of mummies; this rubric names one.

sentences.l: spell · of · not · letting · be-shut-in(?) · the-ba · of-a-man · in · the-necropolis
sentences.i: Spell for not letting a man's ba be shut in(?) in the necropolis.
sentences.n: Spell 91 begins, and Budge's line numerals start again at 1. The papyrus writes rꜣ n tmt rdi ḫni·tw in red, bꜣ s in black, m in red (with a short overline of its own) and ẖrt-nṯr in black. tmt is t, the sledge tm (U15, drawn with crossbars) and the owl m as complement, with a second t, as in Spell 44; rdi is the mouth r and the arm (D36, no loaf), here without the t of the infinitive. ḫni·tw is ḫ, water n and the reed i, then a small irregular blob with an upturned end that could not be identified (Aa2 is a placeholder code), taken as classifier, and t and the chick w: the passive sḏm·tw·f after rdi. As in Spell 30B the signs give ḫni, and the word is taken as a writing of ḫnr 'restrain, shut in', the r written as i; the reading is uncertain (Budge: χenà-tu, 'to be shut up'). bꜣ s 'the ba of a man' as in Spell 61. ẖrt-nṯr has the flag and the loop r (coded D21, approximate) side by side over the block ẖr. The ba must be free to leave the tomb and come back: this spell keeps it from being held at the gates.

sentences.l: said · by · the-Osiris · Ani · O · High-One · whom-one-adores · great · of-might · Ram · great · of-dread
sentences.i: Said by the Osiris Ani: O High One who is adored, great of might, Ram great of dread,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in in red; the rest is black. ḏd in wsir ꜣny as before; ꜣny has the kneeling man with an arm raised as classifier. i 'O' is the reed and the man with hand to mouth. qꜣ 'high one' is the hill q with a man with both arms raised (A28) as classifier, the ꜣ not written. dwꜣ·tw·f is the star dwꜣ (N14) with ꜣ, the coil w, a man with his arms raised in praise (A30) and the roll, then ·f and the t and chick w of tw: the passive sḏm·tw·f, 'one adores him', used as a relative, 'whom one adores'. The suffix ·f is written before tw and read after it, and the coil after the star, which may belong to the stem, is not read (Budge: ṭuau-f-tu). wr bꜣw 'great of might' is wr (the swallow with r) and three jabirus with the seated god and a stroke: bꜣw, the plural of bꜣ, used for the might or power of a god. bꜣ 'the Ram' is the bowl (R7) before a walking ram (coded E10, approximate); Budge's tiny tick over its back is not coded. ꜥꜣ šfšft 'great of dread' is the column ꜥꜣ with ꜥ and the roll, and šfšft, the pool š (coded N37, approximate) and the viper f twice, t, and a recumbent horned animal (coded E10, approximate), the roll and a stroke as classifiers (Budge: śefśeft). The god called on is the sun god, whose ba was the ram.

sentences.l: who-puts · fear-his · in · the-gods · who-appears · on · throne-his · great
sentences.i: who puts the fear of him into the gods, who appears in glory on his great throne:
sentences.n: dd 'who puts' is the arm with a conical loaf (D37) twice: the participle of rdi, its d written twice, as in other parts. nrw·f 'fear of him' is water n, r and the chick w, with a small curled sign on the low hooked sign (the vulture-head curl, coded G14, approximate) and a stroke as classifiers, and ·f. n nṯrw 'into the gods' is water n and the flag three times. ḫꜥ 'who appears in glory' is the hill with the rising sun ḫꜥ (N28) with ꜥ and the roll: the participle. ḥr nst·f wrt 'on his great throne': ḥr is the face; the first sign of nst is printed like the hatched block the type uses for ẖr and is coded T28 as the nearest shape (approximate); then t and a house sign (O1), and ·f. Budge reads nest, and ḫꜥ ḥr nst·f 'who appears on his throne' is the usual phrase, so the seat sign ns is taken as meant: the doubt is in the shape of the printed sign, not a slip the signs could show, and the reading rests on Budge and the phrase. wrt 'great' is the swallow with r and t, feminine to agree with nst.

sentences.l: may-make-he · the-way · for · the-spirit · for · the-ba · of · the-Osiris · Ani
sentences.i: May he make the way for the spirit and for the ba of the Osiris Ani.
sentences.n: ir·f 'may he make' is the eye ir and ·f: the sḏm·f for a wish. wꜣt 'way' is the road with shrubs (coded N31, approximate), t and a stroke. n ꜣḫ n bꜣ 'for the spirit, for the ba': water n before each, and the crested ibis ꜣḫ alone (Budge's tiny tick at its head is not coded). wsir is written here with the tall seat (Q1) before the eye. The ꜣḫ, the spirit, and the ba are two forms in which the dead person lives on, and both need a road out of the tomb.

sentences.l: (iw)-I · equipped-am-I · I · a-spirit · equipped
sentences.i: I am equipped; I am an equipped spirit.
sentences.n: Budge's line 3 begins. iw·i is the reed, the chick and the seated man. ꜥpr·kwi 'I am equipped' is the sign ꜥpr (Aa20, a bag on a cord) with r as complement and the roll, and the basket k: the stative of ꜥpr 'equip, provide', its ending written with k alone (Budge supplies [uà] in his transliteration only). ink ꜣḫ ꜥpr 'I am an equipped spirit': ink with a noun, the ibis ꜣḫ with the long-wigged figure holding a flail (coded A52, approximate) as classifier, and ꜥpr again, here an adjective after its noun. An equipped spirit has the spells and the knowledge it needs in the world below.

sentences.l: have-made-I · the-way · to · the-place · which · Ra · Hathor · (are)-there
sentences.i: I have made the way to the place where Ra and Hathor are.
sentences.n: ir·n·i 'I have made' is the eye ir, water n and the seated man: the sḏm·n·f. wꜣt 'the way' as before. r bw nty … im 'to the place where … are': nty here has no suffix, and its subject, rꜥ ḥwt-ḥr, follows it. rꜥ 'Ra' is the seated god with the sun on his head (C1). ḥwt-ḥr 'Hathor' is one sign, the falcon inside an enclosure (O10): 'the house of Horus', the name of the goddess (Budge: Ḥet Ḥeru). Budge's numeral 4 stands before it, and his '[and]' is in his English only. To reach the place of Ra and Hathor is to join the sun in the sky.

sentences.l: if · is-known · spell · this · (iw)-he · becomes-he · as · a-spirit · equipped · in · the-necropolis · not · is-shut-in(?)-he · at · door · any · of · the-West · in · going-in · in · coming-out · (of)-Nu(?)
sentences.i: If this spell is known, he becomes an equipped spirit in the necropolis; he is not shut in(?) at any door of the West, in going in and in coming out of Nu(?).
sentences.n: The rubric. The papyrus writes all of it in red except ꜣḫ and ẖrt-nṯr, which are black. ir rḫ rꜣ pn 'if this spell is known': ir 'if', rḫ the mouth r, the placenta ḫ and the roll, the passive sḏm·f with its noun subject; pn 'this' is p and n. iw·f ḫpr·f 'he becomes': iw·f, then the scarab ḫpr with r and ·f, the sḏm·f. m ꜣḫ ꜥpr 'as an equipped spirit', the owl m 'as'. m ẖrt-nṯr has the bar m (Aa15). n ḫni·tw·f 'he is not shut in(?)' is the negative arms (D35, approximate) and ḫni·tw as in the title: ḫ, n, the reed and a tall upright with a forked top (coded O30, approximate), the house's sign in this word, the low hooked sign, t, the coil w and ·f. ḥr sbꜣ nb 'at any door': the single sign is a door in its frame (coded O32, approximate), read sbꜣ 'door, gate', as in sbꜣw 'the gates' of the West in Spell 30B; Budge reads sebχet, sbḫt 'gateway' (as in Spell 146), which the single sign could also write, and the reading is uncertain. n imntt 'of the West' is water n and imntt. m ꜥq m pr 'in going in, in coming out' is the bar m twice, the walking legs ꜥq alone, and walking legs facing the other way (coded D55, approximate; D54 is possible) for pr. nw is the pot nw, a stroke and the sky sign: taken as Nu, written with the sky as classifier as in Spell 17, 'out of Nu'; Budge has 'of the sky', and the reading is doubtful.

sentences.l: spell · of · opening · the-tomb · to · the-ba · to · the-shadow · going-forth · by · day · having-power · over · the-legs
sentences.i: Spell for opening the tomb to the ba and to the shadow, for going forth by day and having power over the legs.
sentences.n: Spell 92 begins, and Budge's line numerals start again at 1. The whole title is written in red. wn 'opening' is the hare wn (E34) with water n as complement, and the hatched door leaf (coded O31, approximate) over the low hooked sign (U15) as classifiers: the infinitive. is 'the tomb' is the reed i as complement, a tall bundle of reeds (coded M40, approximate), the sign is, the folded cloth s as complement, a curved plant (coded M2, approximate) and a house sign as classifiers (Budge: àsi). n bꜣ n šwt 'to the ba and to the shadow': water n before each. šwt 'shadow' is the sunshade šwt (S35) with t, printed low before it, a stroke and an oval with two small tabs (coded Aa2, approximate) as classifier. Budge reads χaibit, ḫꜣybt, another word for 'shade' written with the same sunshade; with only t written either reading is possible, and šwt, the usual word for the shadow beside the ba, is taken. prt m hrw 'going forth by day', the phrase that names the whole Book: prt is the house pr with r, t and the walking legs, the infinitive of pri; hrw 'day' is the courtyard h, r and the sun with a stroke. sḫm m rdwy 'having power over the legs': sḫm is the sceptre sḫm (coded S42, approximate) with m and the low hooked sign; m 'over'; rdwy 'the two legs' is the leg (D56) twice, two strokes y and the chick w, the dual. The shadow, like the ba, is a part of the person that can leave the body; both must be let out of the tomb.

sentences.l: said · by · the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani · true-of-voice · the-enclosure(?) · is-opened · what-is-sealed · is-sealed(?) · lying-down
sentences.i: Said by the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice: The enclosure(?) is opened; what is sealed is sealed(?), lying down(?).
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in in red; the rest is black. sš 'scribe' is the scribe's palette with its pen-case, as in Ani's title in the published parts (Budge reads the sign ān, an old value; his 'scribe' agrees). mꜣꜥ-ḫrw is written short. wnt is the hare wn with n, t and a house sign: a noun from wn 'open', taken as a word for the tomb, 'the enclosure'; the sense is doubtful (Budge: unt, 'the place of restraint'). wn·ṯi 'is opened' is wn with the door leaf and the low hooked sign, then the tether ṯ and the reed: the stative, its ending written ·ṯi as for the second person, taken here as the third person feminine ending ·ti, agreeing with wnt. ḫtm 'what is sealed' is ḫ and t with the seal on its cord (S20), the sign ḫtm, and the low hooked sign: ḫtm 'seal, shut', here as a noun. ḫtm·ṯi is the same word with the owl m and the ending ·ṯi: 'is sealed'. Budge has 'that which is shut is shut'; how the second pair fits is not clear, and one may suspect that the sealed thing is the tomb that is now opened. sḏr 'lying down' is the bolt s, a small crenellated sign tied at the neck where Budge reads t' (coded V33, approximate), r, and the lion-legged bier (coded A55, approximate): the verb sḏr 'lie down, sleep', written here without the sign ḏr of Spell 89.

sentences.l: the-enclosure(?) · is-opened · for · ba-(my) · which-is-in-it
sentences.i: The enclosure(?) is opened for my ba, which is in it.
sentences.n: wnt wn·ṯi as in the line before. n bꜣ 'for (my) ba': the jabiru with the bowl at its foot; no sign for ·i is written, only Budge's small tick beside the bird, which is not coded, and 'my' is supplied from the sense (Budge: ba-à). imy·s 'which is in it' is the crossed planks im with m and two strokes y, the nisba imy, and the bolt ·s, 'it' being the enclosure. The ba lives in the tomb with the body and goes out through the opened door.

sentences.l: the-Eye · of-Horus · binds(?) · me · which-makes-firm · the-ornaments · on · the-brow · of-Ra
sentences.i: The Eye of Horus binds(?) me, she who makes firm the ornaments on the brow of Ra.
sentences.n: Budge prints seśeṭu-à as one group; it is split here into sšd and wi (q re-indexed). irt ḥr 'the Eye of Horus' is the eye with t and a stroke and the falcon. sšd is a looped cord (coded V6, approximate) for sš and the hand d: the word seen in Spell 93, here taken as a verb, 'bind, wrap(?)', its sense doubtful (Budge: 'I have bound'); with no suffix it is read as a participle after its noun, 'the Eye of Horus (is the one who) binds'; a feminine participle agreeing with irt would have t, as smnt has, so the form is doubtful. wi 'me' is the chick w and the kneeling man with an arm raised: the dependent pronoun, as object. smnt is the bolt s, the game board mn (Y5) with n and the roll, and t: the feminine participle of smn 'make firm, establish', agreeing with irt. Budge's numeral 3 stands before ḫkrw 'the ornaments', which is a flower on a horizontal stalk (coded M12, approximate) for ḫ, the basket k, r and the chick w, with an ornament of the frieze ḫkr (coded Aa30, approximate) and the roll: the noun from ḫkr 'adorn' (Budge: χakeru, 'splendours'). m wpt rꜥ 'on the brow of Ra': wpt is the horns wp (F13) with t and a stroke, as in Spell 17. The Eye of Horus is here the uraeus on the sun's brow, the snake that guards the god and is worn as his crown.

sentences.l: are-stretched · the-strides · hasten(?) · the-knees
sentences.i: The strides are lengthened; the knees hasten(?).
sentences.n: pd is p and the hand d with a long bar whose ends turn down, the bow (coded T10, approximate), as classifier: pḏ 'stretch', written with d for ḏ (Budge: peṭ). nmtt 'the strides' is the walking legs over t and a stroke; the signs nm are not printed, and the legs stand for the whole word (Budge: nemmat). pḏ nmtt, 'stretch the strides', is to stride out. wn is the hare wn with n and the walking legs: wn 'hasten', the verb of motion written with the legs, as in Spell 46; Budge has 'are lifted up', and the sense is doubtful. mꜣsty 'the knees' is the sickle mꜣ drawn as a hook on the vulture ꜣ, s and t, with the leg twice for the dual (Budge: mast, 'the thighs'). The legs that were bound in the tomb move freely again.

sentences.l: have-made-I · way · this · great · flesh-my · is-firm
sentences.i: I have made this great way; my flesh is firm.
sentences.n: ir·n·i 'I have made', the sḏm·n·f, as in Spell 91. wꜣt pw ꜥꜣ 'this great way': pw is p and the chick w, the demonstrative after its noun; ꜥꜣ 'great' is the column ꜥꜣ lying over the arm ꜥ, with ꜣ and the roll. Both are written in the masculine, though wꜣt is feminine (tw and ꜥꜣt would agree). iwf·i 'my flesh' is the reed, the chick w, the viper f and the flesh sign (coded F51, approximate) with plural strokes, and ·i (Budge: àuf-à, 'my members'). Budge's numeral 4 stands before rwd 'is firm', the mouth r, the chick w and the hand d, with a loop crossed by a stick (coded T12, approximate) and the roll: rwd 'be firm, strong', a later spelling of rwḏ, in the stative.

sentences.l: I · Horus · who-protects · father-his
sentences.i: I am Horus, who protects his father.
sentences.n: ink ḥr 'I am Horus': the falcon with the seated god. nḏ 'who protects' is a stick with a knotted cross-shaped top (coded Aa27, approximate), the sign nḏ, with the pot as complement for its n and the low hooked sign: the participle of nḏ 'protect, take care of'; nḏ itf·f, 'protector of his father', is the title of Horus as the son who stands up for Osiris. itf·f 'his father' is t and the viper f, the i not written, and ·f; Budge prints the second viper, the suffix, in square brackets, as restored.

sentences.l: bring-(I) · the-Great-Crown · at · word-his
sentences.i: I bring the Great Crown at his word.
sentences.n: in 'bring' is the sign in (coded W25, approximate) with water n: the verb ini, its subject 'I' not written (Budge supplies [I]). wrrt 'the Great Crown' is the swallow wr with r, a second r and t, with a crown with plumes (coded S8, approximate) standing on a basket as classifiers (Budge: ureret). m mdw·f 'at his word' is the owl m and mdw, a tall pointed staff (coded S43, approximate), the sign mdw, with the hand d (coded D46, approximate) and a stroke, and ·f. mdw is both 'staff' and 'word'; Budge takes it as the staff, 'upon its staff', and m mdw·f, 'at his command', is the other reading. The son brings his father the crown of a king.

sentences.l: is-opened · the-way · of · the-bas
sentences.i: The way of the bas is opened.
sentences.n: wn 'is opened' is the hare with n, the door leaf and the low hooked sign: the passive sḏm·f, or the infinitive as a heading, 'opening'. wꜣt 'the way' and n bꜣw 'of the bas', the jabiru with the bowl and a dotted stroke, the plural.

sentences.l: (iw) · ba-my · (f) · sees-it · the-god · great · within · the-boat · of · Ra · (on)-the-day · of-the-bas
sentences.i: My ba sees the great god within the boat of Ra on the day of the bas.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes f after bꜣ·i; read without it. iw bꜣ·i mꜣꜣ·f 'my ba sees': iw with a noun and the sḏm·f, a statement of what is so. After bꜣ·i the papyrus has the viper f with two strokes (Budge prints '(sic)' under it, after his numeral 5); it has no place in the sentence and is not translated, perhaps the ·f of mꜣꜣ·f begun too soon. mꜣꜣ·f is the sickle set over the eye, two vultures and ·f. nṯr ꜥꜣ 'the great god' as before; here the plate changes (Plate 18). m-ẖnw 'within' is printed as one group: the owl m and ẖnw, the belly of an animal ẖ (coded F32, approximate), water n, the pot nw and the chick w, with a house sign. wiꜣ n rꜥ 'the boat of Ra': in wiꜣ the vulture ꜣ is Budge's restoration in square brackets. hrw bꜣw 'on the day of the bas' is the courtyard h, r and the sun with a stroke, and bꜣw; 'on' is not written, and the same day is called 'the day of the reckoning of the bas' in line 9.

sentences.l: (iw) · ba-my · comes(?) · in · the-front · among · those-who-reckon · years
sentences.i: My ba comes(?) at the front, among those who reckon the years.
sentences.n: iw bꜣ·i as before; Budge's numeral 6 stands before the second iw, the reed and the chick, which is taken as the verb iwi 'come' (written without the walking legs), 'my ba comes'; it may instead be a second iw, written twice, and the sense is then 'my ba is at the front'. m ḥꜣt 'in the front' is the owl and the forepart of a lion ḥꜣt with t and a stroke. m-m 'among' is the owl m and a second owl joined to the arm ꜥ in one ligature; the arm, from the later spelling with ꜥ (as in the Address after Spell 125), is not read. ip 'who reckon' is the reed, p and a flat roll (coded Y1, approximate): the participle of ip 'count, reckon'. rnpwt 'years' is the palm rib rnp (M4) with t and plural strokes. Those who reckon the years are perhaps the gods who count out the lifetime of each person.

sentences.l: come · have-bound(?)-I · ba-my · the-Eye · of-Horus · which-makes-firm · ornaments-my · on · the-brow · of-Ra
sentences.i: Come! I have bound(?) my ba; (it is) the Eye of Horus that makes firm my ornaments on the brow of Ra.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes n-mn; read smn. mi 'come!' is the owl with the arm in one ligature, which Budge prints in square brackets as restored, the reed and the walking legs: the imperative, written as if mꜥ, as in Spell 17. sšd·n·i is the looped cord sš (coded V6, approximate), the hand d and the low hooked sign, water n and ·i: the sḏm·n·f, 'I have bound(?)' (Budge: seśeṭ-nà, 'hath delivered for me'); the sense of sšd is doubtful. Budge prints n and [s]men as two groups, and they are joined here as one word (q re-indexed): the water n (over which Budge prints '(sic)') stands where the bolt s is needed, then the game board mn with n and a flat roll (coded Y1, approximate); Budge's [s] is in his transliteration only. Read smn, the participle 'which makes firm', as smnt in line 2, here without the t of the feminine. Budge's numeral 7 stands before ḫkrw·i 'my ornaments', written as in line 3 with a stroke and the seated man ·i (Budge's English marks 'my' sic). m 'on' is the bar m; wpt 'the brow' has the flesh sign (coded F51, approximate) as classifier.

sentences.l: light(?) · on · faces-their · those-who-are-in · the-limbs · of-Osiris
sentences.i: Light(?) is on the faces of those who are in the limbs of Osiris.
sentences.n: iḫḫw is the reed, the placenta ḫ twice and the chick w, with the sun with rays falling from it (coded N8, approximate), a stroke and the seated god as classifiers (Budge: àχeχu, 'rays of light'). The classifier shows a word of light; the sense here is taken from it, and the word is doubtful. r ḥrw·sn 'on their faces': r is the mouth r, ḥrw the face with two strokes, and ·sn the bolt, water n and plural strokes. imyw 'who are in' is the crossed planks im, the chick w and a stroke, the plural nisba, in apposition to ·sn. ꜥt wsir 'the limbs of Osiris' is the arm ꜥ, t and the flesh sign (coded F51, approximate) with a stroke, and wsir with the tall seat before the eye. Those who are in the limbs of Osiris are the gods who live in his body; the light of the sun reaches even them.

sentences.l: not · shall-shut-in(?)-you · ba-my · not · shall-guard-you · shadow-my
sentences.i: You shall not shut in(?) my ba; you shall not keep guard over my shadow.
sentences.n: Budge's numeral 8 stands before nn, the negative arms and water n, the negative of the future. ḫni·tn is ḫ, water n and the reed, the forked upright (coded O30, approximate) and a small horned head (coded F1, approximate) with a flat roll (coded Y1, approximate) and a stroke as classifiers, and ·tn, 'you' (plural): the sḏm·f, with the beings about to be named as its subject, and the verb taken, as in Spell 91, as ḫnr 'shut in'. sꜣw·tn 'you shall guard' is the herdsman holding a stick (coded A47, approximate), the sign sꜣw, with the vulture ꜣ written twice as complement and the low hooked sign as classifier, and ·tn; the w is not written (Budge: saa-ten, 'fetter ye'). šwt·i 'my shadow' is the sunshade (coded S35, approximate) with t written before it, a stroke and ·i. The guardians of the world below keep watch over the dead; the spell forbids them to hold the ba and the shadow.

sentences.l: let-be-opened · the-way · for · ba-my · for · shadow-my · may-see-it · the-god · great · within · the-shrine · (on)-the-day · of-reckoning · the-bas
sentences.i: Let the way be opened for my ba and for my shadow, that it may see the great god within the shrine on the day of the reckoning of the bas,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes m-nw; read m-ẖnw. wn wꜣt is written as in line 4, here taken as a wish, 'let the way be opened'. n bꜣ·i n šwt·i 'for my ba and for my shadow' (Budge's numeral 9 stands before the second n). mꜣꜣ·f 'that it may see' is the eye with the sickle at its right and two vultures, and ·f: the sḏm·f after the wish, 'it' being the ba. nṯr ꜥꜣ as before. m-ẖnw 'within' is written here without the belly ẖ: the owl m, the pot nw, three water lines (coded N35A, approximate) and a house sign; only one reading fits. kꜣri 'the shrine' is the raised arms kꜣ, r and the reed, with a shrine (coded O18, approximate) as classifier (Budge: kerà). hrw ip bꜣw 'on the day of the reckoning of the bas': hrw with r and the sun; ip 'reckoning' is the reed, p and a flat roll (coded Y1, approximate), the infinitive in a direct genitive; bꜣw the plural. On that day the bas are counted and judged, and Ani's ba is to stand in the shrine of the god.

sentences.l: may-repeat(?)-it · the-words · of · Osiris
sentences.i: and may it repeat(?) the words of Osiris
sentences.n: nm·f is the knife nm (coded T34, approximate) with the owl m as complement and the roll, and ·f: taken with Budge ('may it repeat') as a verb 'repeat', from the nm of m nm 'again' in Spell 44; the reading is doubtful. ḏdt 'the words, what was said' is a tall tapering sign (coded U28, approximate) for ḏ, the hand d, t and a stroke: the noun from ḏd 'say'. n wsir 'of Osiris': water n, the genitive, and wsir (Budge's numeral 10 stands before it).

sentences.l: to · the-hidden-ones · of-seats · the-guardians · of-the-limbs · of-Osiris · the-guardians · of-the-bas · the-spirits · who-seal-up · over · the-shadows · of-the-dead · who-do · evil · to-me
sentences.i: to those whose seats are hidden, the guardians of the limbs of Osiris, the guardians of the bas and the spirits, who seal (them) up over the shadows of the dead, who do evil to me.
sentences.n: n 'to' is water n: the words are said to the beings who follow. štꜣw 'the hidden ones' is the pool š (coded N37, approximate), t and a small cup with a handle (coded W10, approximate), which carries no sound, as in štꜣ elsewhere in the papyrus, the vulture ꜣ, the chick w and a stroke. st 'of seats' is the seat (Q1) with t, a house and a stroke: štꜣw st, 'hidden of seats', the adjective with a following noun (Budge: àuset). sꜣw 'guardians' is the herdsman with his stick (A47) with ꜣ, w, the low hooked sign and plural strokes, the participle of sꜣw 'guard' used as a noun. ꜥt wsir 'the limbs of Osiris' as before. The second sꜣw has the coil w and plural strokes. bꜣw ꜣḫw 'the bas and the spirits': ꜣḫw is the crested ibis with the long-wigged figure (coded A52, approximate) and a stroke; Budge's numeral 11 is printed inside the next word. ḫtmyw 'who seal up' is ḫ, t, the bar m, two reeds and the seal on its cord (S20) with a stroke: the participle plural of ḫtm 'seal, shut'. ḥr šwt mwtw 'over the shadows of the dead': šwt is the sunshade with t, and mwtw 'the dead' is the bar m (Aa15), t and a small ring (coded N33, approximate), written twice for the plural, and the chick w; Budge reads mitmitu. iryw ḏwt r·i 'who do evil to me': iryw is the eye ir with r, two reeds and the chick w, the participle of iri; ḏwt is the mountain ḏw with t, w, the sparrow and plural strokes; r·i is r and the seated man. The guardians of the bas are named so that the speaker can command them.

sentences.l: not · have-(yet)-done-they · evil · to-me
sentences.i: They have not yet done evil to me.
sentences.n: n is the negative arms alone. irt·sn is the eye ir and t, with ·sn: the sḏmt·f form, which after n strictly means 'they have not yet done'; it is translated so. Budge's 'may they (not) do' takes it as a wish, which this form does not give. ḏwt r·i as before.

sentences.l: pass(?) · the-way · for-me · for · heart-your · (is)-with-you
sentences.i: Make way(?) for me, for your heart is with you(?).
sentences.n: isby is the reed, the door bolt sb on legs (coded O35, approximate), two reeds and the walking legs: sbi 'go, pass', with a reed before it that may be the i sometimes prefixed to an imperative; taken as 'pass on, go by (the way) for me', that is, make way (Budge: àsebi, 'turning away [their] path from me'). The sense is doubtful. wꜣt 'the way' and n·i 'for me' (water n and the seated man). n before ib·k is water n, taken as the preposition 'for, because of', and the rest as a sentence without a verb: ib·k ḥnꜥ·k 'your heart is with you'. ib 'heart' is the heart (F34) with a stroke, the seated god and a dotted stroke, and ·k; Budge's numeral 12 is printed inside the word. ḥnꜥ·k 'with you' is ḥ, n, the arm (printed like the low hooked sign) and ·k. 'Your heart is with you' is said to the dead in other spells as a promise of life; who is addressed here is not clear.

sentences.l: ba-my · spirit-my · equipped · for · going(?)-their · (tw)
sentences.i: My ba and my spirit are equipped for their going(?).
sentences.n: bꜣ·i as before. ꜣḫ·i 'my spirit' is the ibis with the long-wigged figure (coded A52, approximate) as classifier and the seated man ·i. ꜥpr 'equipped' is the sign ꜥpr with r and a flat roll (coded Y1, approximate): the stative, with the two nouns as its subject. n 'for' is water n, which Budge prints in square brackets as restored. The last word is the bolt s, a small bird-like sign (coded G38, approximate), the owl m and the walking legs, then ·sn, then t and the chick w (Budge: sem-sen-tu, 'passage their'). It is taken as sm 'go, make one's way' with ·sn, 'their going'; the bird is not read, and the t and w after the suffix are not explained (they may be the tw of a passive). The reading is doubtful.

sentences.l: sit-I · at · the-head · of-the-great-ones · who-are-foremost · of-seats
sentences.i: I sit at the head of the great ones, who are foremost in (their) seats.
sentences.n: ḥms·kwi 'I sit, I am seated' is the bowl ḥm with its three-pointed rim (coded N41, approximate) and the bolt s, with a wrapped seated figure (coded A47, approximate) as classifier, then the basket k, the chick w and the seated man: the stative with the ending ·kwi. m ḫnty 'at the head of' is the owl m and the water pot ḫnt (coded W17, approximate) with n and t as complements, two strokes y, and the face (D19) with a house as classifiers (Budge prints em and χenti apart and gives 'among' under em). wrwt 'the great ones' is the swallow wr (coded G36, approximate) with r, t and plural strokes, the feminine plural used as a collective (Budge: urt). Budge's numeral 13 stands before ḫntyw 'who are foremost', the pot ḫnt with n, t and two strokes, and st 'seats', the seat with t, a house, the seated god and a stroke; no 'their' is written. To sit among the great gods is the place of an equipped spirit.

sentences.l: not · shall-be-shut-in(?)-you · by · the-guardians · of-the-limbs · of-Osiris · the-guardians · of-the-bas · who-seal-up · over · the-shadows · of-the-dead
sentences.i: You shall not be shut in(?) by the guardians of the limbs of Osiris, the guardians of the bas, who seal (them) up over the shadows of the dead.
sentences.n: nn as before. ḫni·tw·k is written as in line 8, with the low hooked sign after the horned head, then t and the chick w and ·k: the passive sḏm·tw·f, 'you shall not be shut in', 'you' being the ba or the speaker. in 'by' is the reed and water n, the particle that names the agent of a passive. sꜣw 'the guardians' is the herdsman with ꜣ, w and a stroke. ꜥt wsir 'the limbs of Osiris': wsir is written with the eye before the tall seat (coded Q1, approximate), the order of the usual writing in Spells 17 and 18. The second sꜣw has the low hooked sign, and bꜣw the dotted stroke. ḫtm 'who seal up' is ḫ, t, the owl m and the seal on its cord, the participle, here without the plural ending. Budge's numeral 14 stands before ḥr šwt mwtw 'over the shadows of the dead', written as in line 11, the m of mwtw here with the owl.

sentences.l: (is-it-that) · holding(?)-your · (is)-by · the-sky
sentences.i: Is it the sky that holds you(?)?
sentences.n: in iw is the reed with water n and the reed with the chick w: the question particle in with iw, 'is it that …?'. nḏrt·k is water n, the small crenellated sign tied at the neck (coded V33, approximate) where Budge reads t', r and t, with the low hooked sign as classifier, and ·k: taken as nḏrt, a noun in t from nḏr 'grasp, hold' (the infinitive of this verb has no t), 'the holding of you' (Budge: net'ert-k, 'thy place of possession'). in pt 'by the sky': in again, here naming the agent, and pt, p, t and the sky. The question is doubtful in its words and its sense.

sentences.l: if · is-known · spell · this · (iw)-he · comes-forth-he · by · day · not · shall-be-shut-in(?) · ba-his
sentences.i: If this spell is known, he goes forth by day, and his ba shall not be shut in(?).
sentences.n: The closing words of Spell 92 are written in black here, not in red as the rubric of Spell 91. ir rḫ rꜣ pn as before; rḫ is r and the placenta with no roll. iw·f pr·f m hrw 'he goes forth by day': iw·f is the reed, the coil w and ·f, pr·f the house, r, the walking legs and ·f, and hrw is written with the sun and a stroke alone. nn ḫni·tw bꜣ·f 'his ba shall not be shut in(?)': nn with the passive sḏm·tw·f, written as before with the forked upright (O30, approximate), the low hooked sign, t and the coil w, and bꜣ·f with ·f and a dotted stroke. Spell 43 keeps the head on the body; the other three spells of this part ask that the ba and the shadow may go out by day and come back.
